title: Comme Un Dimanche
identity: Michael Mériot, Comme un dimanche for E-flat alto saxophone and piano, A. Leduc AL28141 (1990), about 2:15. The CDMC/Wind Music library catalog classifies it in a conservatory and music-school exam/competition collection and indexes it as Année 1. A Philharmonie de Paris repertoire guide gives additional study-context descriptors; neither source is a score inspection.

evidence.claim: Opened CDMC/Wind Music library catalog record identifies the work for E-flat alto saxophone and piano, A. Leduc, 1990, AL28141, three pages plus a leaf, and duration 2:15. It classifies the item in a collection for conservatory/music-school exams and competitions and assigns the archive’s Année 1 index. This is archive classification, not a SaxoBrain year mapping.

The Philharmonie de Paris ten-year saxophone repertoire guide describes the piece as 3/4 at quarter note = 108, in C for saxophone, with E-flat, B-flat and A-flat accidentals, simple half-, quarter- and eighth-note rhythms, three phrases using an eighth-rest/eighth-note figure, slurred and detached phrasing, soft-to-moderately-loud dynamics (p to mf), and a stated range from low F to high E. These are guide descriptions, not observations from notation.
evidence.source_name: Philharmonie de Paris, 10 ans avec le saxophone repertoire guide

review_focus: The guide describes a moderate 3/4 pulse with simple note values, short eighth-rest-led phrases, slur/detach changes, and dynamics from p to mf. Check the score for how these features are distributed and verify the guide’s stated low-F to high-E range and transposition convention.
